guitar.evidence: Muddy Waters' red Fender Telecaster is iconic and extremely well documented in Chicago blues history, central to songs like 'Hoochie Coochie Man' and 'Mannish Boy'.

tone.target: dirty 60s Chicago blues electric guitar with bite
tone.profile: dirty 60s Chicago blues electric guitar with bite
tone.summary: A classic Chicago blues tone achieved using a British combo amp model (UK 45) for natural break-up, paired with a slight overdrive boost and minimal room ambience to capture the dirty, bite-filled sound of Muddy Waters' era.

rig.name: Muddy Waters - Hoochie Coochie Man - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Add subtle grit and mid-range bite without sounding like modern distortion.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to simulate the slight breakup of an old, overdriven tube amp rather than a dedicated dirt pedal.

alternatives.model: Blues OD (if more warmth is desired)

blocks.purpose: No dedicated distortion needed; the Green OD and amp breakup will provide sufficient grit.
blocks.gap: The 'mustHave' list specifies avoiding fuzz/modern high gain. The natural break-up of the chosen amp model is preferred over a discrete pedal.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the sound of a classic British/American combo amp with natural, mid-forward breakup.
blocks.gap: The UK 45 is chosen for its vintage character and ability to provide grit without modern high gain.
